newsitem.title: USA: USDA seeks up to 7 mln acres for CRP buffer strips.
newsitem.headline: USDA seeks up to 7 mln acres for CRP buffer strips.

text.p: Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman unveiled the National Conservation Buffer Initiative, a public-private partnership to enroll up to seven million acres of farmland as buffer strips.

The land could be converted to anti-erosion, pollution prevention or wildlife habitat uses through the Conservation Reserve or a number of other land preservation programs, Glickman said in a speech to the National Association of Agricultural Journalists.
"This initiative is an effort to use grasses and trees to protect and enhance all the resources on a farm," he said.

Six agribusinesses -- Cargill Inc, ConAgra, Farmland Industries, Monsanto Co, Pioneer Hi-Bred International and Terra Industries -- pledged $1 million over the next three years to promote buffer strips. A half-dozen farm and conservation groups also will participate.
A USDA official said from two to seven million acres of land could be set aside into the strips if the goal of two million miles of strips was achieved. Target date was 2002.
At a minimum, buffer strips must be 20 feet wide and can be up to 80 feet. Some flexibility in size is allowed to assure that a viably shaped field remains for use.
